title: The White Brothers band in Washington and Arthur Whetsol
summary: The White Brothers were a small band of two saxes, trombone, trumpet, drums and bass playing one-nighters, where Tizol first worked with Arthur Whetsol.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, it says '29 to '44. How about the White Brothers Band?

The White Brothers was when I was in Washington; that's what I said, when I was in the pit band in there, and I stayed in Washington, and they dissolved the pit band orchestra; then I was for myself. Then I used to work there with the White Brothers; they made a combination of about five musicians to play at Youngstown and Philadelphia and so forth, doing one nighters. I was with the White Brothers Orchestra.
Who else was in that band? How big an orchestra?
Oh, it was nothing but two saxophones, trombone, trumpet, drum and bass player. It was a small band.
Do you remember who any of the musicians were?
One of the White Brothers was a tenor saxophone; Arthur Whetsol was the trumpet; Tommy Myles was the drummer -- what should I say -- I guess that's about all.
Wasn't Joe Hayman with that band?
You're right. Joe Hayman was the saxophone player, too; he was the alto player -- and one of the White brothers was a tenor saxophone player.
Was that the first time you worked with Whetsol? In the White Brothers Band?

Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's right. Because I used to hear him, and I thought he was terrific. Arthur was a terrific jazz trumpet player. So I worked with Alfred in this particular band. That's about all, I guess.
And then when he went with Duke, he reminded Duke about you?
Because he had worked with you.
And then Duke remembered you from the Howard.
